TOP: Cisco Secure Email Gateway zero-day exploited (CVSS 9.8)
Spacelift puts Cursor agent infra changes under OPA

P.h: Cisco Secure Email Gateway zero-day exploited in the wild
P.p: Cisco's Secure Email Gateway has an actively exploited zero-day, CVE-2026-76519, rated CVSS 9.8. The Register reports unknown attackers are using the 'make-me-root' bug against live appliances.
P.s: Also urgent: Google warns suspected China-linked hackers could mass-exploit a BeyondTrust Remote Support flaw already used in August. Self-hosted customers should apply the BT26-05 patches now, including the precautionary Privileged Remote Access patch.

items.d: Names, addresses, SSNs and driver's license numbers exposed. A hacker claims 7.5M records and leaked a 2.5 GB archive.
Malicious HTML in a repo ran in the preview pane, bypassed the sandbox and stole AWS, GitHub, SSH and OAuth credentials. Patched; update and drop long-lived workstation credentials.
A malicious server can hit remote code execution through a dangling easy handle. Fixed in curl 8.23.0. Found by Anthropic's OSS Scanner.

P.h: Spacelift routes Cursor agent infrastructure changes through policy
P.p: Agent-driven infrastructure changes now flow through Spacelift via a registered Cursor Origin app with a signing key, so the same OPA policies and approvals apply. A cited report says 76% would apply AI-generated Terraform with little review.
P.s: Pulumi ESC also now mints short-lived OIDC tokens for any service, replacing long-lived API keys, and ADK now spans five languages with MCP and A2A support.

tiles.t: Pulumi ESC issues OIDC tokens for any service
tiles.d: fn::open::oidc tokens expire within an hour. Works with Anthropic, Cloudsmith, JFrog Artifactory and Aembit.
